summary: Agent 0.29.0 can trust several operator keys so the signing key can be rotated (ADR-0058, TM-13). UpdateCfg gains public_keys (node-local YAML only; the router provisioning never writes it). trustedKeys() decodes public_key plus public_keys and refuses the whole set if any entry is not a 32-byte Ed25519 key, naming its position, so a typo cannot silently shrink the trusted set; with no key the order is refused as before. verifyOrder accepts the manifest if the signature verifies under any trusted key (signedByAny), then applies the unchanged manifest, version, downgrade (ADR-0054) and file checks; the refusal text 'Manifest-Signatur ungueltig' used by the end-to-end suite is kept. deploy.py gains --new-agent-key and --use-next-agent-key, implemented in the new deploy/agent_keys.py: step 1 refuses without a current key or with a pending next key and creates agent-update.next.key with O_EXCL and mode 0600; step 2 refuses without a prepared key, keeps the old key as agent-update.retired-<time>.key and moves the next key into place; both run offline in the ops folder before any SSH connection. The router's optional single-key self-check is unchanged and documented as switched together with the signing key.

findings.evidence: Agent 0.28.0 trusted exactly one update.public_key, so replacing the signing key required changing every node and the key at the same moment.
findings.resolution: Several node-local trusted keys and two self-checking deploy steps; a rotation has not been practised in the deployment yet, so TM-13 stays open.

limitations: Agent tests ran on Windows locally; Linux and the cross-build run in CI.
The 0600 mode of the next key is checked only on POSIX; the deploy steps were not run against the real ops folder.
The router's optional modes.agent_update.public_key self-check still takes a single key.
